title: Speed Up a Distant Mobile Client
description: A mobile app in Europe calls an API hosted only in the US (round trip about 120 ms). Each screen makes six sequential requests, and the client opens a new HTTPS connection for every request. Server processing takes about 10 ms per request. Which change removes the most latency?

options.text: Switch the payloads from JSON to Protocol Buffers.
options.explanation: Payloads are small, so serialization and transfer time are a tiny fraction of the delay; round trips dominate.

options.text: Move the API servers to larger instances with more CPU.
options.explanation: Server time is about 10 ms per request. Faster CPUs cannot remove network round trips.

options.text: Replace TCP with UDP for the API calls.
options.explanation: UDP drops reliability and ordering, so the API would need its own transport. It is not a drop-in fix; HTTP/3 over QUIC is the standard way to get UDP-based benefits.

options.text: Reuse one persistent HTTPS connection (or HTTP/2) and terminate TLS at a nearby edge, then batch the six calls where possible.
options.explanation: Each new connection costs a TCP and a TLS round trip before the request, roughly 360 ms per call at 120 ms RTT. Connection reuse and edge termination remove most of that, and batching removes sequential round trips.
